The schema lives outside this repo (in `~/projects/entu-research/`, repo `entu/research`, path `docs/schema/v4E/`), so a same-repo PR label or CI check can't guard it from this side. Three options, cheapest first:

**Option A — Commit trailer on the mvox PR that depends on the schema change** (recommended):
- When a PR in `mvox_v4e_web` requires a schema mutation that has already landed (or will land) in `entu/research`, the PR description must include a trailer like:
  ```
  Schema-Change: entu/research@<sha> "<short title>"
  PO-Approved: <date> <PO handle or "verbal in session">
  ```
- I RED any PR whose diff references new/changed v4E entity types, properties, or relations without both trailers.
- Cost: zero tooling. Convention-only. Enforced by me at review.

**Option B — `docs/schema-approvals.md` log in this repo**:
- Append-only log: date, schema element changed, PO approval evidence, link to entu/research commit.
- I RED if the log isn't updated alongside the dependent code.
- Cost: one file to seed; light maintenance.

**Option C — PR label `schema-mutation` + checklist**:
- Requires team-lead to apply the label; checklist item "PO approval recorded" must be ticked.
- Cost: label management overhead, easy to forget. Weakest gate.

My pick: **A + B together** — the trailer makes the dependency visible at review time, the log gives a queryable history. B alone gets stale; A alone leaves no audit trail. Both are convention-only, no tooling.

Open question for PO: does "PO approval" need to be written (e.g., GitHub comment, email) or is in-session verbal acknowledgement (logged by team-lead) sufficient? Cheapest path is "verbal-in-session, logged by team-lead with timestamp"; strictest is "PO must comment on the entu/research PR before mvox PR merges."
